category_title: Silent and depressed EMLLs experiencing extreme language-related frustration and school avoidance
scenario_title: Expressive writing and labeling for a drawing assignment
minimal_context: Jessica is working one-on-one with a volunteer to write an English label for her drawing of a teacher for the classroom bulletin board.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: We need to write an English label for your drawing so we can put it on the classroom bulletin board.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Looks down at her drawing of a female teacher in front of a board, looking reluctant to attempt writing in English) 음…제가 그리고 싶은 그림은요, 제가 선생님이 되어 있는 모습이요. Umm…The picture I want to draw is, myself who became a teacher and teaching my students.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: That is a good idea. Please write that down in English for the label.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Hesitates, holding her pencil but not writing) 저는…나중에 자라서 선생님이 되고 싶다는. 그런 아이디어가 있어요. I want to be a teacher when I grow up. I have an idea like that.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Okay, go ahead and put those English words on the paper now.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Stares silently at the paper, unable to come up with the words in English to write her own label. She puts the pencil down, leaving the label completely absent)

task.content: Labeling a drawing for the classroom bulletin board in English.

context.environment: Weekly reading and writing activities in English and Korean
context.materials: Drawing assignment for the classroom bulletin board, picture of a female teacher in front of a board, chalk in hand

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: Unable to come up with the words in English to write her own label.
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: The absent label was a painfully visual representation of Jessica’s ‘deficit’ in English.
